content.text: A single query can also fetch entries related to the ones it finds: their parents, children and siblings, their translations, the entries they link to and the entries that link to them. Put a relation in `select` (or in `include` when you don't select), and it's resolved in the same query.

Every relation takes the same options as a query, such as `type`, `filter`, `select`, `orderBy`, `skip` and `take`. `parent`, `previous` and `next` return a single entry, the others a list. Add `count: true` to get the number of matches instead, as in `Query.children({count: true})`, or `first: true` to get a single entry (or `null`). Relations can be nested, for example children with their own children.
Tree relations
`Query.parent(...)`: the parent entry, or nothing for entries at the top of a root.
`Query.parents(...)`: all ancestors, starting at the top of the root. Pass `depth` to get only the nearest ones: `depth: 1` is the parent.
`Query.children(...)`: the direct children. Pass `depth` to include deeper descendants too, returned as one flat list.
`Query.siblings(...)`: the other children of the same parent. Add `includeSelf: true` to include the entry itself.
`Query.previous(...)` and `Query.next(...)`: the sibling right before or after the entry, in sidebar order, or nothing at the ends.
`Query.translations(...)`: the same entry in the other locales of the root. Add `includeSelf: true` to include the current locale, listed first.
Tree relations stay in the locale of the entry they start from (except translations, of course) and use the status of the outer query.
`siblings`, `previous` and `next` find entries that share a parent. For an entry at the top level of a root, they find the other top-level entries of the same root (and locale).
Linked entries
Entry
Link
Image
and
File
fields return the basics of what they link to. To get other fields of the linked entries, query through the field:
a single link field has `.first(query)`.
a multiple link field has `.find(query)`, `.first(query)` and `.count(query)`. Results keep the order the editor gave the links.
Linked entries are looked up in the locale of the entry you queried, falling back to entries without a locale, so a link to an untranslated author keeps working from every translation of a post.
Entries that link here

Links are stored on the entry that links. `Query.referencedBy` finds the entries that link to the entry, through any of their fields, including links in rich text. Pass `type` to only find entries of that type, and `field` to only follow one link field of it. Like the other relations it takes the query options, `count: true` and `first: true`:

The entries that link to a translated entry are looked up in its locale. For an entry without a locale, such as a shared author, the linking entries of every locale are returned: pass `locale` to only get those of one locale.

The same relation is a filter condition: `_referenced` holds for entries that an entry of the query links to. `{_referenced: true}` matches entries that anything links to and `{_referenced: false}` entries nothing links to, such as unused media files:
Filtering on the link

The other way around, "the posts by this author" is a filter on the posts: links store the id of their target as `_entry`. This is the way to go when you start from the posts, for example to page through them:
For multiple links, such as categories, use `{categories: {includes: {_entry: id}}}`. More combinations are in
